To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
plant HMGR is regulated by PP2A, and that PP2A is a calcium binding protein that can integrate developmental and environmental signals in the regulation of HMGR.

PP2A is a multilevel regulator, positive or negative, of HMGR in plants, both during normal development and in response to stress conditions, and that the interaction with HMGR occurs through calcium binding proteins, the B" subunits of PP 2A.
PP2A is a positive and negative modulator of the key enzyme of the isoprenoid pathway, HMGR, in plants.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of the mechanisms of action of protein phosphatase PP2A in the regulation of plant HMG-coenzyme A reductase (HMG-CoA reuctase, HMGR), the key enzyme in the biosynthetic pathway of isoprenoids, and with the role of this phosphatase in the control of isoprenoid metabolism in plant cells.
understanding how plants adapt to their ever changing environment and how they are able to maintain their metabolic homeostasis.
understanding the molecular mechanisms by which plants adapt to environmental stress and how they respond to the external signals that trigger stress responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PP2A is a positive and negative regulator of plant HMG-CoA reductases.
PP2A is a key regulator of plant HMGER activity, and the interaction between the two proteins is mediated by B"-type regulatory subunits of the phosphatase.
the plant HMG-Co A reductase is a key enzyme in the mevalonic pathway for isoprene biosynthesis and is modulated by protein phosphatases 2A (pp2a).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PP2A regulates HMGR by phosphorylating it at Ser-863, and that this phosphorylation is modulated by calcium.
the plant PP2A-HMGR system is a key component of the signaling networks controlling the plant mevalonate metabolism.
PP2A is a key regulator in the control of isoprenoid synthesis, which is essential for normal plant growth and for the response to environmental stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PP2A-B" subunits are not just passive carriers of the catalytic subunit, but rather are active participants in the regulation of plant growth, development, and adaptation to stress.
PP2A is a versatile modulator of plant HMGR and, thus, of isoprenoid metabolism.
PP2A, a ubiquitous and evolutionarily conserved phosphatase, is an important regulator of plant HMGER, and its role in this process is likely to be conserved across species.
